project.name: portail-dossiers
project.kind: Case tracking portal with attachments and OIDC sign-in

requirements.summary: Staff create and view cases, upload attachments and track status changes.
drivers: Consistent transactions across cases and their history
Complete CRUD responses within the applicable workshop latency budget; validate with representative data before claiming performance compliance
constraints: No direct browser access to the database or secrets

CRUD list/read/update: preserve the SDI server p99 target <=100 ms per method/route template; >100 to <=350 ms requires justification and >350 ms is outside the contract. A full response is required; job acceptance is not a substitute.

Measure API ingress to final response completion for the CRUD target, with correctness and failures reported separately. The workshop acceptance envelope below is illustrative, not a production observation SLO.
assumptions: Files are served after the API checks permissions
The paths in the plan refer to sources that have yet to be created

This fictional brief states no additional product latency SLO. Proposed test envelope: 10 requests/second for each critical CRUD route, up to 20 concurrent clients, 10,000 cases, paginated responses <=64 KiB, a 15-minute acceptance run with reported warm/cold conditions and sample count.
Proposed outcome criterion for valid test requests: no incorrect result, unhandled server error or timeout in the acceptance run; this is a test criterion, not a future 100% reliability guarantee.

SLO evidence status: proposed and unmeasured. Test the complete path with authorization, representative Postgres data, resource limits, and query/pool telemetry; define a separate upload-size/time contract before adding large-file workloads.

architecture.rationale: Choose a modular monolith because one team owns related CRUD use cases and atomic case/history changes. Keep CRUD synchronous because the brief requires the complete result and the proposed bounded query path is plausible within the course budget; validate it under the declared envelope. Reject microservices without independent ownership/scaling needs and reject a job as a replacement for a complete CRUD response. Reconsider only if evidence or product semantics changes.
architecture.compute_tradeoff: A single synchronous API is sufficient for the expected volume. No queue, worker, durable workflow or LLM call is provisioned.

alternatives.rejection_reason: They would multiply processes and communications for a single team and tightly coupled transactions.
Compatible with the platform, but Django experience and its ORM reduce delivery time here without an additional service.

alternatives.option: Background jobs for ordinary CRUD responses
alternatives.rejection_reason: The operation requires a complete authoritative result. A quick 202 would change the contract; first optimize measured SQL/pool/payload costs if the synchronous path misses its target.

components.runtime: Browser; Vite assets served by nginx
components.rationale: The browser displays cases and calls only the business API.
components.framework_rationale: React enables reuse of the form components the team is familiar with; Vite builds the static assets.

components.rationale: The API checks permissions, coordinates use cases and stores cases and their history in a SQL transaction.
components.framework_rationale: Choose Django because the Python team already maintains its ORM, migrations and validation for transactional CRUD. Prefer it to FastAPI here because no independent async-heavy API or FastAPI-specific capability offsets assembling separate persistence/migration conventions. This is a functional/team decision, not a proven speed advantage. Verify the full CRUD SLO; reconsider the framework only if actual library/concurrency needs or a measured remaining runtime bottleneck change the comparison. Casdoor remains the OIDC provider.
